what_this_is: The cost of the entropy-threshold ask baseline, on four belief arms over the pre-registered decile grid for tau, and the first per-case VoI computation in this project.

sign_is_committed.claim: Every excess reported here is positive because all 400 committed per-case ceilings are negative and the unconstrained-menu maximum is -2/13 in closed form. This gate reproduces the sign as a regression guard and quantifies the magnitude.
sign_is_committed.what_would_be_a_bug: A non-positive excess anywhere. It contradicts a committed invariant, so ceiling_agreement raises rather than reporting it.
sign_is_committed.what_is_new_here: The firing index set per threshold, the cost magnitude, the first computed V_q and VoI, and the finding that the committed ceiling is attained exactly on some pairs rather than merely bounding them.

beliefs.why_four_arms: Matches results/voi-ceiling-arms.json, which this gate reads for the per-case ceilings, so no column is dropped.
beliefs.rebaselined_carries_no_claim: Gate 4's abstention run scored three arms because 'rebaselined would add a column about cache drift, which abstention has nothing to do with' (results/abstention.json beliefs.why_three_arms_not_four). That reason applies to entropy thresholding too. The column is kept for consistency and is a cache-drift column: no sentence in this artifact or the paper rests on it.
beliefs.dev_is_in_sample: The isotonic map was fitted on dev, so calibrated b_h on the dev half is in-sample. Claims are test-only.

adapter.what_it_checks: The six-vector expected cost equals the two-part expected cost on every prior and every action, so it is an adapter over the same cost model rather than a second one.
adapter.why_it_is_needed: src.questions.narrow raises NonFactorisingError on a coupled posterior rather than projecting onto its marginals, so costs.expected_cost cannot be evaluated on one at all. q_specifics produces coupled posteriors on real cases (results/answer-model.json adapter.coupled_example).

definitions.v_act: min over F \ {ask} of EC(a | b)
definitions.why_v_act_inside_v_q: One question, so the agent cannot ask again after the answer. Relaxing that is Gate 6's boundary.
definitions.the_wrong_form: V(b) - V_q(b) - EC(ask | b) is a tautology because V(b) <= EC(ask | b) identically once ask is on the menu. Not computed here.
definitions.constraints_survive_the_answer: A constraint is a case-level fact about what the agent may do, so the same non-ask menu applies at the prior and at every posterior.
definitions.units: Bits select and trip thresholds; cost points score. No bit value is compared to a cost value anywhere in this script.

s4_inventory.tau: deciles of the observed H(b) distribution on the arm being scored, imported from experiments/abstention.py unchanged
h_decimals: derived at Gate 4 against the measured float-noise bound; carried, not re-chosen

tau_grid.why_quantiles_not_absolute_bits: The observed distribution is bunched. An absolute grid over the 0-2.585 bit theoretical range would put most of its points in a region holding almost no cases, which is the S4 failure mode this gate is checking for. Deciles make the step commensurate with the quantity by construction.
tau_grid.declared_incomparability: Decile values are not comparable across arms in absolute bits, because H(b) shifts when b_h shifts. Compare arms at equal quantiles, or read the bit column and accept that the same quantile is a different threshold on each arm.
tau_grid.repeated_tau_are_repeated_thresholds: A decile grid on a tied distribution repeats values. Where two quantiles give the same tau they give the same firing set and the same cost, and the rows are identical by construction rather than by coincidence.
tau_grid.why_the_top_decile_can_fire_on_nothing: The grid is taken over all 100 cases and the scoring is on the 50 test cases. If an arm's highest-entropy case is a dev case, tau at the 100th percentile is above every test case and the firing set is empty. That is the population choice showing through, not a failed comparison.

ceiling_agreement.note: The sign is the committed artifact's, reproduced here as a guard. Its being negative on every case is not a result of this gate.

invariants.what_invariant_6_actually_tests: Less than it looks. Substituting VoI = V_act - EC_ask - V_q into the slack (V_act - EC_ask) - VoI cancels both other terms and leaves V_q, measured above as agreeing to 7.77e-16. So on these definitions the invariant reduces to V_q >= 0, which holds because every entry of costs.COST is non-negative. It confirms the implementation is self-consistent; it is not independent evidence for the bound.
invariants.where_the_independent_check_is: ceiling_agreement, which compares the recomputed EC(ask | b) - V_act(b) against the per-case ceilings committed in results/voi-ceiling-arms.json, and recovers V_act a second way via ceiling + EC(ask). That is what ties this gate's new code to Gate 4's analytic result. It is the check invariant 6 was meant to be: a different invariant, the same intended outcome — this gate's computed VoI held against Gate 4's committed ceiling, per arm, under ceiling_agreement above.
invariants.why_attainment_matters: V_q = 0 exactly on these pairs, so the ceiling is reached rather than merely bounding. A free perfect oracle driving the post-answer expected cost to zero still loses by the full -ceiling, which means the bound's negativity cannot be attributed to slack in the bound.
invariants.what_invariant_4_means_here: Where the non-ask argmin is the same whatever the answer, the answer cannot change the action, so V_q == V_act exactly and the whole ask price is wasted: VoI = -EC(ask | b).

threshold_sweep.firing_rule: ask iff H_q(b) > tau, else the V_act argmin
threshold_sweep.why_firing_sets_are_not_listed: Derivable from per_case h_bits and the tau column, so listing them would be a second copy that could drift from the first.

monotonicity.why_the_tiers_must_be: Nested firing sets and a positive per-case excess. Checked, not assumed: a rise raises.
monotonicity.what_an_inversion_means: A case left the firing set and v1's realised cost on it was dearer than ask-then-act's, so the total rose while the firing count fell. Expected cost is what the ceiling bounds; a single realised draw can go either way, and here it does.

threshold_sweep.why_the_reference_is_per_arm: realised_excess_over_v1 is measured against this arm's own v1-policy total, above, not against published's 86. v1's policy on rebuilt beliefs scores 70 on raw and 75 on calibrated; charging those arms an excess against 86 would compare them to a total they never had.
threshold_sweep.expected_ledger: tier1 and tier2 are expected cost under the belief. Tier 1 is answer-model-free because V_q >= 0 for any answer model; tier 2 uses the Gate 3 table.
threshold_sweep.realised_ledger: realised_total_cost scores against the labels, exact in expectation over the answer, and is the only column comparable to v1's committed total. An expected excess added to a realised total would be neither.

gate5_all_test_cases_ask_then_act.pricing: C(ask, s) + C(a_u, s), expected over P(u | s_true)

always_ask_anchor.why_they_differ: Terminal pricing charges the ask and stops; ask-then-act charges the ask and then the action the answer selects. Equality on every case would mean the follow-up is free everywhere, which is a bug.

self_consistency.name: self-consistency check of the implementation
self_consistency.not_a_validation: The answer is simulated from the same P(u | s) that produced the prediction, so this is circular with respect to the answer model by construction. It checks arithmetic, not reality.
self_consistency.seed_is_not_a_defence: The seed makes the number reproducible. It does nothing about the circularity above and is not offered as if it did.
self_consistency.external_validation: none; the Limitations entry is the paper gate's

question_selection.oracle: argmax_q VoI(q | b) over the three real questions
question_selection.argmax_ig_is_secondary: answer-model-dependent and ordering-fragile: 27 of 88 sweep variants flip the IG ordering of these three questions (results/answer-model.md), so it carries no headline.
question_selection.q_null_excluded_from_the_oracle: IG identically 0 at full ask price, so an oracle allowed to pick it could choose a dominated question. Kept in by_question as the zero-information reference.
